AcceptInvitationRequest.title: AcceptInvitationRequest

CurrentSession.title: CurrentSession

DecisionOut.description: A decision, with the moment it was taken.
DecisionOut.title: DecisionOut

DeclareMeetingRequest.description:
EF-40: the desktop announces that a recording has started.

Sent at the beginning, not the end. A laptop that dies mid-meeting then
still leaves a row to reconcile against.
DeclareMeetingRequest.title: DeclareMeetingRequest

DeletionScheduled.description:
EF-06: the answer to a deletion request.

Both instants are returned because the difference is the whole point: the
request is recorded now, the data disappears later, and until then the
customer can change their mind.
DeletionScheduled.title: DeletionScheduled

ExportedAuditEntry.description: One audit entry inside an export (section 21.2).
ExportedAuditEntry.title: ExportedAuditEntry

ExportedInvitation.description: One invitation inside an export. The token itself is never included.
ExportedInvitation.title: ExportedInvitation

ExportedMember.description:
One member inside an export.

Deliberately not a `MemberSummary`: an export is a durable file the
customer keeps, so it carries the settings that would be needed to
recreate the account. It carries no password hash, no TOTP secret and no
token — an export is handed over, and a credential in it would outlive
every revocation.
ExportedMember.title: ExportedMember

FinalizeRequest.description: Every part is uploaded; assemble the object and queue the work.
FinalizeRequest.title: FinalizeRequest

FinalizeUploadRequest.description:
The local manifest: what the desktop is about to upload.

Sent once the Opus file is encoded and hashed, before a single byte leaves
the machine. The size is what determines how many presigned slots come
back, so it has to be the real one.
FinalizeUploadRequest.title: FinalizeUploadRequest

InvitationCreated.description: What the inviter gets back. Never the token: that went to the invitee.
InvitationCreated.title: InvitationCreated

InviteMemberRequest.description: EF-03: invite someone into the organization, with a role.
InviteMemberRequest.title: InviteMemberRequest

LoginRequest.title: LoginRequest

MeetingDetail.description: A meeting with everything the player needs.

MeetingSummary.description: A meeting as the API returns it.
MeetingSummary.title: MeetingSummary

MemberSummary.description: A member as listed to an administrator.
MemberSummary.title: MemberSummary

OrganizationExport.description:
EF-06: everything the organization owns, in one document.

`format` is a version string rather than a number so a reader can tell at
a glance what it is holding. Meetings, reports and the audio manifest join
this document when those tables exist (lot L2), which is why the version
is stated in the file rather than assumed by whoever opens it.
OrganizationExport.title: OrganizationExport

PasswordResetConfirm.description: EF-02: consume the link and choose a new password.
PasswordResetConfirm.title: PasswordResetConfirm

PasswordResetRequest.description: EF-02: ask for a reset link.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

ReportOut.description: The structured report of one meeting.

TaskOut.description: A task, with what was said about its deadline and what that resolves to.
TaskOut.title: TaskOut

TokenPair.description:
What a successful authentication returns.

The refresh token is opaque and single-use: presenting it returns a new
pair, and presenting it a second time revokes the whole family.
TokenPair.title: TokenPair

TranscriptSegmentOut.description: One diarised passage, as the player shows it.
TranscriptSegmentOut.title: TranscriptSegmentOut

UpdateMeetingRequest.description:
What a human may change about a meeting.

Status is absent on purpose: it moves through the state machine, never
through a request body.
UpdateMeetingRequest.title: UpdateMeetingRequest

UpdateOrganizationRequest.description:
EF-05: organization settings an administrator may change.

Plan, quota and status are absent: they are billing state, changed by the
payment flow and never by a customer request (ADR-09).
UpdateOrganizationRequest.title: UpdateOrganizationRequest

UpdateProfileRequest.description:
EF-04: what a user may change about themselves.

Every field is optional: a client sends only what it is changing, and
omitting a field leaves it alone. Role is absent on purpose — nobody
promotes themselves.
UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest

UploadPart.description: One presigned slot, to be filled with a chunk of the recording.
UploadPart.title: UploadPart

UploadTicket.description:
Everything the client needs to upload, and nothing else.

The URLs are bearer credentials with a short life: whoever holds one can
write that part until it expires. They are handed to a caller who has
already been authorised, and never logged.
UploadTicket.title: UploadTicket

UploadedPart.description: What the store returned for one part, echoed back at finalisation.
UploadedPart.title: UploadedPart

UserProfile.description: EF-04: the profile the web and desktop apps display.
UserProfile.title: UserProfile

VerifyEmailRequest.title: VerifyEmailRequest

WebSocketTicket.title: WebSocketTicket

info.summary: Meeting capture, transcription and structured reports.
info.title: NovaBrief API

post.description:
EF-02: for the link that never arrived, or expired.

Authenticated, so it names no address and cannot be used to send mail to
someone else.

EF-02.

Unscoped, and deliberately unauthenticated: the link arrives in a mail
client and is followed in whatever browser is open, which is usually not
the one holding a session.
post.summary: Confirm an email address from its link

post.description:
EF-03: one click, which creates the account.

Unscoped: the organization is only known once the invitation is found.

Signing out revokes the whole family this token belongs to.

Answers 204 whether or not the token was known: a different answer would
tell a caller whether a token they hold is still live.
EF-02: single-use, 30 minutes, and every session is revoked.
post.summary: Set a new password from a reset link

post.description:
EF-02.

Always 202, whether or not the address exists. This endpoint needs no
credential, so a different answer would turn it into a way to test which
addresses are customers.
Presenting a token consumes it; presenting it twice revokes the login.

EF-01: one step, and the creator becomes Owner.

Also sends the EF-02 verification link. A delivery failure does not fail
the signup; see `auth.register`.
post.summary: Create an account and its organization

get.description:
EF-04 and EF-05: the profile and the organization behind it.

Built by the shared presenter, so this and `PATCH /me` cannot drift.

patch.description:
EF-04. Any caller, on their own account only.

There is no `PATCH /users/{id}`: the target is always the token's subject,
so no request can name someone else.

get.description:
Newest first.

RLS scopes this to the organization; no tenant filter is written here. The
caller is passed for the one thing RLS cannot express — a colleague's
private meeting is inside the same tenant and still must not appear.

schema.title: Response Index Api V1 Meetings Get

post.description: EF-40: called when recording starts, and returns the `debug_id`.

delete.description:
Author or administrator.

A state, not a `DELETE FROM`: the consumption record has to keep a meeting
to point at (section 19.2).

get.description:
A meeting in another organization answers 404, not 403.

RLS makes the two indistinguishable, which is what stops the endpoint from
confirming that an identifier exists somewhere else.

patch.description: Author or administrator. Title and privacy only.

post.description: The author changed their mind, or the recording was a mistake.
post.summary: Abandon a recording before it is queued

post.description:
EF-40: 202 in under 500 ms, and the user never waits on a request.

The size the store reports is checked against the size declared at
`finalize-local`. A truncated upload is refused rather than transcribed
into a confident, incomplete report.
post.summary: Close the upload and queue the processing

post.description:
Section 16.4: the local manifest goes in, upload slots come out.

The audio never passes through this API. The client writes straight to the
bucket with the URLs below, which is what keeps a small server from
becoming a file proxy for hundreds of megabytes.
post.summary: Hand back presigned slots for the recording

get.description:
Everything the player needs (EF-52).

The audio link is presigned and short-lived, and absent once the recording
has been purged (ADR-06) — a null there is a normal answer, not an error.
get.summary: The report, the transcript and a link to the audio

post.description:
EF-45's Retry button. Author or administrator, and only from FAILED.

Resumes at the stage that failed rather than from the top: a meeting whose
transcript survived goes straight back to analysis.

EF-18: an outage outlives a fifteen-minute signature.

Nothing changes here — not the state, not the key, not the upload. The
parts the store has already accepted keep their numbers, so the client
sends what is missing rather than the meeting again.
post.summary: Sign the upload slots again, for an upload already under way

post.description:
Section 17.2.

A browser cannot set an Authorization header on a WebSocket, and a token in
a query string ends up in every access log. This grants one thing, once,
for sixty seconds: watching this meeting's status.
post.summary: A single-use ticket for the status socket

delete.description:
EF-06. Owner only, and nothing is destroyed yet.

202 rather than 204: the request is accepted, the deletion happens later.
A 204 would tell the client the data is gone, which for the next seven days
is untrue.

patch.description: EF-05. Admins and Owners only; the tenant comes from the token.

post.description: EF-06: the retraction. Owner only, within the seven days.

get.description:
EF-06. Admin or Owner.

Not restricted to the Owner: an administrator can already read the members
and the settings through this API, so an export gives them no reach they
did not have. Deletion is a different matter and is Owner-only.

Served inline as JSON with a filename, so a browser saves it rather than
rendering it into the address bar.
RLS scopes this to the caller's organization; no filter is written here.
